subject: Human Evolution
title: The Neander Valley Skull
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Neander Valley Skull.

hook.text: In 1856, quarry workers in Germany's Neander Valley found a strange skullcap with a heavy brow ridge.

buildup.text: Local teacher Johann Fuhlrott recognized it wasn't modern human. Scientists called it a deformed idiot.

discovery.text: It was the first recognized fossil of another human species—Homo neanderthalensis.

twist.text: Similar skulls had been found before but discarded. Nobody knew what to look for until this one.

climax.text: The Neanderthal find launched paleoanthropology—the scientific study of human origins.

punchline.text: A quarry accident birthed a science.

quiz.question: Where was the first recognized Neanderthal fossil found?
